feedback:
Written before this candidate has raced. Evidence: iteration 4 (kp 1.5, kd 0.15, ki 0, base_speed 1.4, last_direction, x = +/-0.03, 16 mm) scored 53.71 with max_error of 0.0607, 0.0648 and 0.0621 m and one line loss per trial. Iterations 3 (ki), 5 (line_loss), 6 (base_speed 1.25, 54.14 best so far) and 7 (kp 2.0, 53.40) each left that excursion essentially unchanged. Iteration 2 showed that the wider +/-0.05 spread cut progress on the s-bend and slalom (0.04 and 0.035, against 0.16 and 0.11), so the spread should stay near +/-0.03. This candidate is a single-variable test against iteration 4: outer spacing goes from +/-0.03 to +/-0.025, with the inner sensors and the footprint at 0.016 m. The geometry is valid and the change is small. Its expected effect is modest, and it is not obviously broken. Racing is more informative than another revision round, since all designs so far score within about 1.5 points and have shown no completions.

What to do next, depending on the race telemetry. (a) If max_error and line_loss_events are unchanged (about 0.060 to 0.065 m, one loss per trial), outer spacing is not the limit. Do not spend more iterations on gains, speed, footprint or spacing. Test a body or drivetrain variable instead, such as wheel_track 0.10 (narrower track, higher yaw rate per PWM difference) or mass 0.6. (b) If progress falls below about 0.11 or steering_oscillation rises with no gain in max_error, revert spacing to +/-0.03. (c) If max_error drops to 0.06 m or below, or line_loss_events falls on some seeds, keep +/-0.025 and combine it with base_speed 1.25, which was the best raced score (iteration 6). Check progress and completion_time before adding any other change.
